result.summary: Independently re-verified BACKEND-DEV's REQ-030 implementation (walk-in registration at the door, message-text-as-state-carrier confirm/override mechanism) against docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md section by section, re-deriving the verdict myself rather than trusting the backend-dev handoff's report. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md in full, then read apps/bot/src/domain/walkin.ts (decideWalkinOutcome, commitWalkin, parseWalkinArgs/validateWalkinFields, normalizePhoneForMatching, the format/parse message pair) and apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.ts line by line. Confirmed: decideWalkinOutcome implements §5's exact 7-row first-match-wins table in the stated order; commitWalkin implements §6.2's exact 10-step sequence -- events row locked FOR UPDATE first, phone match resolved inside the SAME transaction (getUserIdByPhone run against tx, not db), person resolved-or-created (createWalkinUser sets consent_pd_at on the SAME INSERT per S1, never a separate later write), existing registration row locked FOR UPDATE, admittedCount/seatsLeft computed fresh (never trusted from an earlier tap -- each commitWalkin call opens its own transaction with its own fresh locked read, confirmed by reading the function: no seatsLeft/admittedCount value is ever passed in from the caller), decide, then exactly one write (UPDATE or INSERT) plus exactly one writeAuditLog call per outcome branch, with the audit action chosen by the seatsLeft/overrideConfirmed table (registration.checkin / registration.walkin_admit / registration.walkin_override_admit) matching §6.2 exactly. getUserIdByPhone (domain/user.ts) matches §3.4 exactly -- a declarative SQL-side regexp_replace digit-strip comparison, never an application-level string compare. createWalkinProfile (domain/profile.ts) matches §6.4 exactly -- only first_name/company/phone set, company '' converted to NULL, every other column left at its default. 2. Test-count discrepancy (flagged in this run's task) fully resolved: checked out master's actual commit at branch-cut (707617e, REQ-029's squash-merge commit) directly and ran the full suite myself -- 29 files / 293 tests, NOT the 286 BACKEND-DEV cited as pre-change baseline. Root cause: REQ-029's own pipeline shows REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER signed off at 286 (28 files), but TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 (handoffs/WF02-REQ-029/step-04-test-runner.json) added a new committed test file (checkinQr.forgery.test.ts, 7 cases) AFTER that gate, bringing the true final count to 293/29 -- confirmed again by RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own independent run (handoffs/WF02-REQ-029/step-05-release-validator.json: '29 files / 293 tests'). BACKEND-DEV cited the earlier, superseded 286 figure instead of running against the actual master HEAD. This is a baseline-reporting error, not a lost/skipped-test problem: 293 (correct master baseline) + 7 (this branch's own walkin.db.test.ts) = 300, exactly the current total, which I verified myself (see commands). No test coverage is missing anywhere; git checkout of 707617e was done read-only for verification and immediately reverted (git checkout HEAD -- . then git checkout feature/WF02-REQ-030), confirmed clean before continuing. Logging this as a MINOR issue against BACKEND-DEV's verification discipline (cite the actual current master HEAD count, never a remembered/prior-gate figure) -- not blocking, since the actual total and diff are both correct. 3. Independently re-verified every AC with my own fixtures (own tgId band 949_000_00x, own chapters/events/phone values, calling commitWalkin/parseWalkinArgs/validateWalkinFields/requireOrganizerForChapter directly against the same scratch Postgres, written to apps/bot/scratch-reviewer-req030.ts, run, then deleted -- git status confirmed clean before and after): - AC1: parsed+validated a fresh command's args and asserted commitWalkin is never reachable without a Confirm tap (mirrors the design's own structural argument in §8.1 step 7); captured users/profiles/registrations counts before and after -- byte-identical. PASS. - AC4: two commitWalkin calls with the same physical number in two different formats ('+7 (701) 222-33-44' vs '77012223344') against two different events for the same organizer -- second call resolved to the SAME user/profile row (byte-identical users/profiles counts across both calls), the existing profile's company was left untouched, and two registrations (one per event) exist for that one user. PASS. - AC5: ran a real commitWalkin admit with phone '+998971234567', then read EVERY row in audit_log (not just the one this flow wrote) and JSON-stringified each row to search for the raw phone value or the AC4 fixture's own digit string -- zero matches across the whole table. PASS. - AC3: filled a capacity-1 event's only seat via one commitWalkin call, then called commitWalkin again for a second person with overrideConfirmed=false -- returned 'needs-override-confirmation' with zero registration rows written (confirmed dismiss-equivalent: never calling commitWalkin again leaves the row count unchanged); then called commitWalkin a second time with overrideConfirmed=true -- admitted with exactly one registration row and exactly one registration.walkin_override_admit audit row. PASS. - AC6: seeded a plain member (role='member') and gave them an EventStaff row for the event (the exact AC6 negative shape: EventStaff grants check-in rights, not admission rights) -- called requireOrganizerForChapter directly, got { ok: false, reason: 'not-organizer' } (not 'wrong-chapter', confirming the refusal is role-based, not merely chapter-scoped), zero rows written. PASS. All five independently reproduced with fixtures distinct from walkin.db.test.ts's own (different tgId band, different chapter codes, different phone numbers/company names). 4. Confirmed requireOrganizerForChapter (domain/eventAuthorization.ts, REQ-016), not requireEventStaffForEvent, gates this flow at all three points: read eventAuthorization.ts's checkOrganizerForChapter directly -- role='member' always refused with 'not-organizer' regardless of any EventStaff row, matching S2's stricter requirement (admission is a seat-granting decision, not a check-in-only one). Confirmed all three call sites in handlers/walkin.ts (command handler §8.1 step 5, confirm callback §8.2 step 4, override callback §8.3's inherited step 4) call requireOrganizerForChapter, never requireEventStaffForEvent -- grepped both handler and domain files, requireEventStaffForEvent does not appear anywhere in this diff. 5. Confirmed no domain logic leaked into handler bodies (decision 0004): read handlers/walkin.ts in full -- it only parses ctx, resolves lang/event, calls requireOrganizerForChapter/parseWalkinArgs/validateWalkinFields/parseWalkinMessageFields/commitWalkin, and routes the returned outcome.kind to a reply. No admission/capacity/decision logic of its own; every decision is delegated to domain/walkin.ts's pure decideWalkinOutcome or commitWalkin's already-decided outcome. domain/walkin.ts itself imports no grammY symbol (confirmed via its own import list -- drizzle-orm, db/schema, i18n/catalog, and sibling domain modules only). 6. Confirmed no now()/current_timestamp inside any time-dependent predicate: grepped domain/walkin.ts for now()/current_timestamp -- the only hits are a code comment restating the rule (lines 15-16), not an actual call. decideWalkinOutcome takes evaluationTime as an explicit parameter; commitWalkin takes at as an explicit parameter and passes it straight through to isFinished/writeAuditLog/the registrations write -- the DB clock is never consulted inside a predicate. 7. No schema/migration change in this diff (git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts is empty, no new migration file) -- SECURITY-REVIEWER's S13 migration-review gate does not apply. 8. No new npm workspace, no build-output relocation, no workspace script rename in this diff (git diff master...HEAD -- package.json apps/bot/package.json apps/web/package.json Dockerfile is empty) -- the Docker-build re-verification step in my own role file does not apply; skipped on that basis, not silently. 9. Scope: every changed/new file (apps/bot/src/domain/{walkin,user,profile}.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/{walkin,walkin.db.test}.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,en,ru}.ts, apps/bot/src/index.ts) is named in docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md's own file list; no out-of-scope files touched. No design-system token/component concern -- apps/bot has no visual/CSS surface (restated correctly in design §13, consistent with REQ-016/017/018/028/029's own precedent). Commands run myself, real output, repo root: `npm run lint` -> exit 0, apps/bot 0 problems, apps/web 2 pre-existing unrelated -element warnings only (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx). `npm run build` -> exit 0, apps/web Next.js/Turbopack build clean (4/4 static pages), apps/bot tsc clean. `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite) -> 30 files / 300 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported total exactly. Checked out master at 707617e (read-only, reverted immediately after) -> 29 files / 293 tests passed -- the real, correct baseline (see item 2 above). `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.db.test.ts` -> 1 file / 7 tests passed, my own re-run. Own scratch script `apps/bot/scratch-reviewer-req030.ts` (written, run, deleted) -> 22/22 independent assertions passed across AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6.

issues.title: BACKEND-DEV's REQ-030 pre-change test-count baseline (286) was stale
issues.description: BACKEND-DEV's step-02 handoff reported 'up from the pre-existing 286 tests before this branch's changes', but master's actual HEAD at branch-cut (707617e) is 29 files / 293 tests -- 286 was REQ-029's own count as of its REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER gates, before REQ-029's own TEST-RUNNER step added 7 more tests (checkinQr.forgery.test.ts) that were folded into the same squash-merge commit. The actual current total (300) is correct and no coverage is missing -- this is purely a citation of a superseded number, not a regression. Route: BACKEND-DEV should verify baselines against the actual current master HEAD via a fresh checkout/run, not a remembered figure from an earlier gate in a prior requirement's own pipeline.
